extracted.intended_audience: military lawyers, War Department officials, and legal researchers dealing with U.S. Army retirement law
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of legal standards and interpretive rulings governing retirement, advancement, duties, privileges, and limitations of U.S. Army officers on the retired list under various statutes and regulations (early 20th-century context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential approval required for retirement on examining board findings
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer cannot be retired on the findings of an examining board unless the President approves such findings; approval of the Secretary of War is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See footnote: 'An officer can not be retired on the findings of an examining board unless the President approve such findings. The approval of the Secretary of War is not sufficient.' (citing 21 Op. Atty. Gen., 385, July 31, 1896).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination when incapacity discovered after examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If after successful passage of an examination for promotion, and before promotion, an officer becomes incurably insane or otherwise incapacitated, the War Department may order a second physical examination or place him before a retiring board; prior favorable findings do not bind the Department to await promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: I B 6 d — approval of a favorable finding did not bind War Department to await promotion; officer might be given a second physical examination or ordered before a retiring board. (C. 28852, Aug. 14, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory form of oath for examining-board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations prepared under legislative sanction prescribing the manner in which examining-board members must take the oath are sufficiently mandatory that failure to take the oath as prescribed warrants disapproval of the board's proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent swearing of the members does not cure the defect indicated in the record. (I B 6 e (1); C. 20588, Oct. 25, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of finding and vacancy on transfer to retired list
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examining board convened under the act of Oct. 1, 1890, finds an officer incapacitated and the finding is approved, and that officer is senior in his grade with a vacancy in the next grade, this transfers the officer from active to retired list and places him in retired-status operations under sections 1255 and 1257 R.S.; once legally accomplished, the Executive lacks power to restore the officer to the active list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-contributed causes of incapacity may justify retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of habits (e.g., morphinism) contributed to sufficiently by incidents of the service can warrant the President in exercising discretion to place the officer's name on the retired list even if the condition is not in line of duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I B 6 f (1); example: morphine given for neuralgic pain later resulting in chronic morphinism—retirement upheld. (C. 22809, Apr. 16, 1908).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to board of review and statutory promotion/suspension sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examining board (under April 23, 1908 as amended) finds an officer not professionally qualified for promotion, proceedings should be referred to a board of review. If the review disapproves the examining board, the officer is entitled to promotion; if the review approves the finding of unfitness, statute requires suspension from promotion for one year with later reexamination, and upon a second similar failure, retirement without promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement under April 23, 1904 — service 'otherwise than as a cadet' required
rubrics_metrics.description: The April 23, 1904 act permits advancement in retired rank for officers who 'served with credit as an officer or enlisted man, otherwise than as a cadet' during the Civil War; service as a cadet/midshipman that did not otherwise participate does not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I C 1 a,b; holdings distinguishing midshipmen/cadets who did or did not 'actually participate' in operations against the enemy. Cases: C. 19271; C. 16271, 16409, 22459.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement inapplicable for service as civil employee or contract surgeon
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer on the retired list cannot be advanced in grade under the April 23, 1904 statute because of service performed as a civil employee or as a contract surgeon, regardless of assimilation to commissioned service or oath of allegiance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I C 1 c,d; C. 16312, 16672 and related citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia service not called into U.S. service does not qualify for advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Service as a militiaman not called into the service of the United States and thus not serving in the Regular Army or volunteer forces is not creditable for advancement under the April 23, 1904 act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-martial conviction before Apr. 9, 1865 does not bar advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers on the retired list who served otherwise than in the Volunteers and who were convicted by courts-martial preceding Apr. 9, 1865 are nonetheless subject to advancement under the April 23, 1904 act; conviction does not render service not creditable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers deceased at time of consideration cannot be advanced
rubrics_metrics.description: The April 23, 1904 authorization to advance certain retired officers does not operate in the case of a deceased officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers retired under Oct. 1, 1890 may be advanced under Apr. 23, 1904
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer retired under the act of Oct. 1, 1890 may be advanced in grade on the retired list under the act of Apr. 23, 1904, in appropriate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement effective date is notification of approved action
rubrics_metrics.description: When an officer is found incapacitated for active duty, he passes to the retired list on the date when he is notified of the approved action of the retiring board in his case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement orders generally cannot be revoked or modified to relate to another statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an officer has been retired pursuant to the requirements of a statute authorizing such retirement, the order effecting that retirement cannot later be revoked or modified so as to make the retirement relate to another statute, even if multiple statutes applied at the time of retirement; action cannot be reopened by a new Secretary of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I E; C. 16416, May 27, 1904 et seq.; earlier precedents cited (P. 41, 358; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform and title limited to actual rank
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer is not authorized to wear any uniform other than that of his actual rank nor to be addressed in orders or official communications by any title other than that of his actual rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I F; C. 9826, Feb. 14, 1901. Section 34 of Feb. 2, 1901 does not repeal section 1212, U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officers do not exercise public office (except when assigned statutory duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired officers (except when assigned to duty under section 1259 R.S. or other statutes) do not exercise public office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on assisting in pension claim evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In the sense of section 5498 R.S., a retired officer may not assist a regular soldier in obtaining the evidence necessary to support his application for a pension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officers subject to trial by court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired officers, being part of the Army, are subject to trial by general court-martial independently of specific statutory provisions; retirement does not prevent trial for offenses committed prior to retirement within applicable limitation periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I G 2 b; R.33, 613 (Dec. 1872); C. 25574, Sept. 14, 1909. Some punishments (suspension, loss of files/relative rank) are not appropriate to a retired officer's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to Government Hospital for the Insane and transportation expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired officers are entitled to admission to the Government Hospital for the Insane upon a commitment issued by the Secretary of War; expenses of furnishing a military escort are a proper charge against Army transportation appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military authority may restrain retired officer leaving jurisdiction to avoid civil proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a retired officer is about to leave the United States to avoid civil proceedings (e.g., alimony), the military authority may legally require him to remain within the jurisdiction of the civil court to protect the service's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired pay exempt from state taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the same principle exempting U.S. officer pay from state taxation, the salary of a retired Army officer is equally exempt from state taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officer 'holds office' within certain statutory senses
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer holds office within the meaning of section 1223 R.S., which provides for the vacation of his office by accepting/holding certain appointments (e.g., diplomatic or consular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I G 2 f; G. 14444, Dec. 15, 1911. Multiple cases and opinions discuss whether retired officers 'hold office' for various statutory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding federal office and salary incompatibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer may hold any federal office to which he is elected or appointed, but he may not accept any position incompatible with his status as a retired officer; generally he cannot accept an office whose salary exceeds $2,500 per year except in limited statutory exceptions (e.g., appointment by President with Senate consent, certain engineering positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I G 3 a (1) and (2)(6); citations: C. 14399, Apr. 8, 1903; 19353; 2301 (Member of Congress permitted). The act of July 31, 1894 (28 Stat. 205) imposes the $2,500 limit but contains exceptions for retired officers under certain appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding diplomatic/consular offices; volunteer/militia appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired Army officers are precluded from holding diplomatic and consular offices by section 1223 R.S.; governors may appoint retired officers to commissions in volunteer forces provided their retired pay is less than $2,500 annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I G 3 a (2)(a)(b); cases: C. 4051, Apr. 25, 1898; 22500, Dec. 19, 1907. Section 2 of July 31, 1894 recognizes presidential appointments with Senate consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officers may hold State offices absent contrary State statute
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer may accept any State office unless a State statute forbids it; examples include mayor or member of State legislature, though holding certain militia duties may create incompatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I G 3 b; C. 3327, June 30, 1897; other cited decisions and limitations (e.g., incompatibility when on State militia duty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officers may act as counsel before courts-martial and receive fees
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no objection to a retired officer acting as counsel for an officer before a court-martial or retiring board and to receiving agreed fees or other compensation from his client.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statutory provision for burial expenses of retired officers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no law or regulation authorizing payment of burial expenses of a retired officer; Army regulation limiting burial expense payments to officers who die 'when on duty' at a post does not include retired officers who die at a military post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active duty assignment vs. active service distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of a retired officer 'to active duty' under statutes (e.g., Apr. 21, 1904) is distinct from being on the 'active list' or 'active service'—a retired officer detailed to active duty remains on the retired list and is not thereby restored to active service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I K 1: status of active duty for retired officers is temporary and does not remove them from retired list; see C. 24306, Feb. 25, 1909; 23623; 23760.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'staff duties not involving service with troops' limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'staff duties not involving service with troops' contemplates only staff duties connected with the existing military establishment; the law cannot be read to authorize detail of retired officers on full pay to duties such as familiarizing themselves with pending litigation to appear as witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on assigning retired officers to staff department core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual emergencies, retired officers should not be assigned to perform staff duties which, under law, officers of staff departments are expected to perform; assignments reviving rank or causing friction (e.g., serving under juniors) are inexpedient and not recommended—assignments to civilian-equivalent inspector roles may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarters and housing when retired officer on active duty
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer on active duty without troops is to be furnished quarters in kind after hospital staff quarters have been provided; if no quarters remain, authority to hire necessary quarters should be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired officers eligible for certain courts and inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Under statute and precedent, retired officers may, with consent, be appointed members of courts of inquiry and general courts-martial; courts composed entirely of retired officers may be convened to try officers and enlisted men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rules for retired officers on college duty
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer detailed on college duty under section 1225 R.S. is regarded as on active duty for certain statutory pay rules and is entitled to his full retired pay unless he is a colonel or lieutenant colonel, in which case he receives full pay and allowances of a major on the active list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of retired officers to colleges in territories
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1225 R.S. is permissive with respect to Territories; an officer on the active or retired list may be assigned to duty at a college or university in the Philippine Islands with minimum capacity requirements; application to Porto Rico also recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow's six-month pay limited to officers on active list
rubrics_metrics.description: The act authorizing six months' pay to the widow of an officer who dies on the 'active list' does not extend to a retired officer assigned to 'active duty' under Apr. 21, 1904; such a retired officer is not an officer of the 'active list' within the meaning of the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quartermaster sales/issue of furniture to retired officers restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: A Quartermaster may not issue or sell to retired officers furniture purchased under the act of May 11, 1908 even if the retired officers are on active duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to longevity pay after retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers on the retired list are entitled to longevity pay which had accrued prior to retirement; exception for those retired on account of wounds received in battle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mileage and witness fees claims of retired officers
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer's claim for mileage may be disallowed if he delays traveling to his home beyond a reasonable time after retirement; however, a retired officer subpoenaed as a witness before a general court-martial is entitled to mileage and witness fees of a civilian witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I M 1 and I M 2; example disallowance C. 2978, Mar. 1897; entitlement as witness C. 19611, Apr. 28, 1906; see XV Comp. Dec. 235.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement for pre-existing mental incapacity permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer may be wholly retired for being 'mentally incapacitated for performing the duties of an officer of the Army' even when such incapacity does not result from service but from natural causes existing prior to entry into military service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to full and fair hearing before Army retiring board
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1253 U.S. entitles an officer subject to retirement to a full and fair hearing before an Army retiring board upon due summons if he demands it, including appearing with counsel, introducing testimony, and cross-examining witnesses (including medical members). Failure to appear when summoned waives the right to a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I N 2; historical precedents R. 23, 626 (Aug., 1867); 31, 603 (Aug., 1871); waiver consequences noted.
